vectors.source: TLC counterexample, model v1 (trace reconstructed by hand from the TLC state dump)
vectors.note: keyLog was keyed by (sid, ctr) only; a ratchet session has one sending chain per direction, so a1->b1 ctr 1 and b1->a1 ctr 1 on sid 1 are different keys. Fixed by keying on (sid, sender, ctr).

vectors.source: TLC counterexample, model v2 (trace from TLC output)
vectors.note: The newly linked device b3 did not hold the AccountControlState that linked it, so it believed itself revoked and dropped a1's message. Fixed: the linking ceremony hands the new device the authorizing state. MULTI_DEVICE_SYNC.md 'new-device bootstrap uses an explicit grant' implies this but does not say the grant must carry the control-state head.

vectors.source: TLC counterexample, model v3 with all rules K1..K9 enabled
vectors.note: a1 initiates sid 1 (prekey message m2) then sends m1 on sid 1 without the prekey header; m1 overtakes the prekey message, b1 cannot decrypt, requests a reset, a1 marks sid 1 stale and retries on sid 2, then the delayed prekey creates sid 1 at b1: b1 prefers 1, a1 prefers 2. Led to rule K10 PrekeyUntilConfirmed (Signal's PreKeySignalMessage behaviour). Q-050 does not state it.
vectors.expect_with_fixed_model: trace infeasible after step 5 (m1 carries the prekey header and creates the session)
